title: THE REGULATIONS FOR THE GUILT OFFERING

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'These are the regulations for the guilt offering, which is most holy: The guilt offering is to be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood is to be splashed against the sides of the altar.'" - Lev 7:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once again God attaches those two words to an offering born out of failure: most holy.

The guilt offering was brought by someone who had stolen, cheated, lied under oath, or damaged what belonged to another. It was the offering of the person who had genuinely wronged someone. And God ranks it among the holiest things at His altar.

We would not have written it that way. We would have put the offerings of praise at the top and quietly filed the reparation offering at the bottom.

But consider what was actually happening. A person who could have kept quiet has come forward. A person who could have kept the money has brought it back. A person who could have protected his reputation has admitted what he did. That kind of honesty is rare and costly, and God honours it.

Jesus told a story of two sons. One said he would go and work and did not. The other refused and then went. Which of the two did what his father wanted? (Mtt 21:31). The second — the one who changed course.

God is not looking for people who never fail. He is looking for people who come back.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I see coming back to God after failure as shameful, or as something He honours?
2. Is there a wrong I could put right that I have been avoiding out of embarrassment?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that returning to You is holy in Your sight, not humiliating. Give me the courage to come back quickly. Amen.
